updates.title: Sustainable Land Preparation Begins for AfriNuts Cashew Farm in Odienné
updates.excerpt: AfriNuts launches Phase 1 of its agroforestry project in Ivory Coast, implementing eco-conscious land preparation for 35 hectares of cashew cultivation.
updates.content: AfriNuts has initiated sustainable land preparation on its 50-hectare Odienné property, with 35 hectares designated for cashew agroforestry. The process, led by certified environmental contractors, includes selective vegetation management (Aug 15–Oct 1, 2025) using low-impact techniques to preserve topsoil and biodiversity. All cleared biomass will be repurposed as organic mulch or through controlled biochar production (Oct 2–20), eliminating open burning. Firebreaks will follow permaculture principles to minimize ecosystem disruption. The project avoids deforestation by retaining 30% of native tree cover as windbreaks and wildlife corridors, with planting aligned to regenerative agriculture standards for the 2026 rainy season (May–June).
updates.author: Hamza S. Ralsan Sangare

updates.title: Partnership with Local Farmers Cooperative
updates.excerpt: AfriNuts signs a long-term partnership with the Odienné Cashew Growers Association to support 200 smallholder farmers through training, technical assistance, and market access.
updates.content:
AfriNuts Export is proud to announce the signing of a long-term partnership with the Odienné Cashew Growers Association, a union of over 200 smallholder farmers in the northern region of Côte d’Ivoire.

This partnership represents a critical pillar in our inclusive growth strategy, designed to empower farmers while strengthening the foundation of our vertically integrated value chain.

Through this collaboration, AfriNuts will provide:

A. Training in sustainable and regenerative farming practices, tailored to local conditions and aligned with organic certification standards
B. Technical assistance and agronomic support, including access to high-quality planting materials
C. Guaranteed purchase agreements at fair and transparent farm-gate prices, reducing market volatility and ensuring long-term income security for participating farmers

By year three, the program aims to significantly increase yields while maintaining the region’s organic integrity. In addition to productivity, the partnership will place a strong emphasis on:
1. Post-harvest handling improvements to reduce loss and enhance product quality
2. Gender-inclusive agricultural practices that ensure equitable participation and benefit distribution
3. Shared learning platforms between AfriNuts agronomists and cooperative members to foster long-term knowledge exchange

A Personal Reflection from the Field

During my recent visit to Côte d’Ivoire, I had the opportunity to sit with every single one of the farmers, not just the growers themselves, but also the elders and community leaders. What struck me the most wasn’t just their warmth, hospitality, or respect, it was their unanimous desire to partner with us.

Every last family expressed interest in supporting AfriNuts and playing a role in building this venture from the ground up. The level of trust and hope they placed in us was humbling.

One of the most powerful moments came in the village of Sokraba, where we met with the respected leader Chaka Koné, the chief of the village. He personally gifted us a plot of land, a generous, heartfelt gesture, so we could begin building our first local storage and training facility right there in their community. The atmosphere was filled with joy and anticipation. We were not seen as outsiders. We were welcomed as brothers.

This wasn’t just a business meeting. It was an affirmation of what AfriNuts stands for: shared growth, community-first partnerships, and African-led development.

This partnership is not just an operational milestone, it is a human one. Together with the Odienné Cashew Growers Association, we are walking forward with purpose, and we invite others who believe in ethical, sustainable agribusiness to walk with us.

Sekou Hakim Peters
Co-Founder & Quality Control Lead
AfriNuts Export
updates.author: Sekou Hakim Peters
